Comparing webpack's output with oxc's on the `benches/full` bundles shows three.js still larger, mostly from shader source kept as strings. terser writes every tab in a string as `\t`, which takes two bytes. A raw tab is legal inside any quoted string and takes one. The `improve` phase now writes tabs raw when:

- the string is quoted, not a template literal;
- it is at least 100 characters long;
- it holds at least two tabs.

The limits come from gzip. Writing every tab raw made d3, echarts, terser, typescript and vue slightly larger gzipped. Limiting it to two or more tabs fixed those bundles, but 53 test262 cases still grew by 1–4 bytes gzipped. With the 100-character minimum added, none of the 80 affected corpus cases is larger gzipped. An escaped backslash before a `t` (`\\t`) is left as it is.

```js
// var s = "uniform float t;\n\tvoid main(){\n\t\tgl_FragColor=vec4(t);\n\t}\n\t// a shader long enough to pass the length check, padded out here"; console.log(s, "a\tb");
// before
var s="uniform float t;\n\tvoid main(){\n\t\tgl_FragColor=vec4(t);\n\t}\n\t// a shader long enough to pass the length check, padded out here";console.log(s,"a\tb");
// after (each tab below is one raw tab character)
var s="uniform float t;\n	void main(){\n		gl_FragColor=vec4(t);\n	}\n	// a shader long enough to pass the length check, padded out here";console.log(s,"a\tb");
```

Minified against `main`, the 12 real-world bundles in `benches/full` (`passes: 2`, mangled):

| Bundle | raw | gzip |
| --- | --: | --: |
| three.js | −3,901 (652,863 → 648,962) | −77 (159,140 → 159,063) |
| all 12 | −3,901 (10,081,168 → 10,077,267) | −77 (2,355,290 → 2,355,213) |

The other 11 bundles are byte-for-byte unchanged. CPU time and heap on the bundles are within run-to-run noise (35.5–37.5 s on both branches, about 595 MB heap). The corpora pass with no exclusion entry added. The first commit removes an swc exclusion that `main` no longer needs; #22510 carries the same commit.
